analysis.title: Weekly Economics: Thoughts of the Week - Strength in Employment Settles December Rate Debate
key_insights: Raymond James expects the Fed to raise the federal funds rate by 25 basis points at the December FOMC after the strong October payrolls report, and to stay on hold throughout 2027.
October nonfarm payrolls rose 165,000, above expectations. The unemployment rate fell to 4.1% from 4.2% and the 3-month average gain rose to 137,000 from 79,000.

Professional and business services added 70,000 jobs in October against a roughly 15,000 monthly average over the prior year. The authors say statistical noise may be inflating the figure and will keep monitoring.

BLS and ADP diverged on manufacturing and construction. BLS showed manufacturing +19,000 and construction -3,000, while ADP showed manufacturing -1,000 and construction +13,000. The authors attribute part of the gap to different samples, and tie construction strength to the data-center boom.

The authors argue current inflation has different drivers than the post-pandemic surge. Growth is led by an AI and data-center investment cycle supported by immediate expensing and by wealth gains from higher equity prices, not by broad consumption.
Consumer sentiment and confidence remain weak relative to growth because the benefits are concentrated in investment and asset ownership.
The authors disagree with the Fed Chair's statement that 'inflation is a choice'. They say bringing inflation down, or doing so faster, is the choice.
The bottom line is that investors should focus on whether investment-led growth can keep offsetting tighter monetary policy and uneven consumer confidence in 2027.

ISM Manufacturing PMI rose to 55.5% in October from 54.5%, the 10th straight reading above 50. Production rose to 59.0% and prices eased to 75.2% from 77.9%. Sentiment among respondents worsened for the 3rd month, with the Iran war cited in 21% of comments.
Construction spending fell 1.9% m/m in September, below expectations, and 2.7% y/y. Home renovations drove the weakness, while data-center construction spending rose 8.6% m/m.
JOLTS job openings rose to 7.5 million in September from an upwardly revised 7.19 million. The openings rate rose to 4.5% from 4.3% and the hires rate to 3.4% from 3.3%.
ADP private employment rose 86,000 in October, above expectations and equal to September. Earnings growth for job-changers hit its fastest pace since March 2024.
The trade deficit narrowed 0.7% to $105.0 billion in September. Capital goods imports rose $11.6 billion, which the authors read as a sign of a strong AI and data-center cycle.
ISM Services PMI fell to 54.5% in October from 54.9%, slightly below expectations. New orders dropped to 55.9% from 59.8% and prices eased to 73.0% from 74.0%.
Q3 productivity rose 3.6% q/q and unit labor costs fell 0.7%, the first decline since Q2 2025. The labor share of output was 53.0%, the lowest since 1947.

University of Michigan preliminary November sentiment rose to 51.0 from 48.0. 12-month inflation expectations fell to 4.3% from 4.7%. Sentiment fell among households with the largest stock holdings, and 57% cited high prices.

The Raymond James forecast table shows the fed funds upper bound at 3.75% in 4Q25-2Q26 and rising to 4.00% in 3Q26 and 4.25% from 4Q26. Year-end averages are 3.9% for 2026 and 4.3% for 2027, with CPI at 3.5% in 2026 and 2.9% in 2027.

sector_views.rationale: Hiring was well above trend in October, but the authors suspect statistical noise and are waiting to see if it persists.
Data-center construction is strong while residential renovation spending is weakening sharply.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Broad-based job growth that supports a December rate hike.
Down from 4.2% in September, with participation up slightly to 61.9%.

risk_factors: Tighter monetary policy and uneven consumer confidence may weigh on investment-led growth in 2027.
Persistently high input prices: ISM manufacturing prices at 75.2% and services prices at 73.0%.
Concern over a possible AI bubble among consumers, per the Michigan survey.
Weakness in residential renovation and construction spending.
Tariffs, longer lead times and the Iran war weigh on manufacturer sentiment.
vol_and_positioning: Michigan sentiment fell among consumers with the largest stock holdings, reflecting high stock market volatility.
geopolitical: The US-Iran war is cited in 21% of ISM manufacturing respondent comments as a source of disruption.
Michigan sentiment is 10% lower than in February, just before the start of the Iranian conflict.

tension_points.bull_case: A resilient labor market and a powerful AI and data-center investment cycle, supported by immediate expensing and household wealth gains, keep the economy growing.
tension_points.bear_case: Tighter monetary policy and uneven consumer confidence could drag on growth, because the benefits are concentrated in investment and asset ownership rather than broad consumption.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The report does not state a specific level or event. It says investors should watch whether investment-led growth can keep offsetting tighter policy and weak consumer confidence in 2027.

theme_stances.key_argument: Strong October payrolls settle the December FOMC debate, so the authors expect a 25 basis point hike.
theme_stances.evidence: We expect the Fed to raise the federal funds rate by another 25 basis points.

theme_stances.key_argument: Growth is driven by an AI and data-center investment cycle rather than broad consumption, which likely explains weak consumer sentiment.
theme_stances.evidence: growth is being driven by a powerful investment cycle tied to artificial intelligence
